scope: The original canonical-subject fixture uses checked manual support/coquotation/usage APIs. failures: The initial standalone 512 MiB Lean compiler limit was below the imported environment requirement; the bounded 1536 MiB build passed.
The first combined build retained an older Live source because the copy list omitted it; the build copy list now explicitly includes Live and Import.
Changing pinned Prepared from a Head to its actual Snapshot exposed one fallback constructor; it was corrected.
Adding the optional timestamp required explicit Entry.mk arguments at existing test call sites.
The linker response initially deduplicated every argument, incorrectly removing repeated -L options. The response now preserves all linker options and their order.

The first regression run passed the native rebuild and age tests, then failed linking the newly covered Import suite because its object was not in the link response; the response now includes that actual object once.
Earlier canonical-subject and automatic reconstruction failures remain in their raw guards and preceding committed review.
The existing long source test required maxRecDepth=2048 for elaboration; the failing build is retained.

A source regression reconstructed an old demand request without the current synaptic identity. Physical memo rows existed. The fixture now validates production-published request/response/source/dependency records instead of inventing a partial key.
The new test helper initially compared Except values without a BEq instance; corrected through checked Option values.
Initial indexed-array and complete-knowledge proofs, namespace qualification and record syntax were corrected in the retained failed builds.
The first native usage target fixture used obsolete selection/origin accessors; the fixture was corrected.

The first full native usage regression found ACK reconstruction projecting merged file spans rather than original rows. Reconstruction now checks each original row, retaining exact partial gaps and general-data ACK unions.
